newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "wise man" recommends two-year EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German "wise man" recommends two-year EMU delay.

text.p: A key adviser to the German government was quoted on Monday as saying a delay of two years to Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) would be preferable to the introduction of a weak euro in 1999.

"If one is divided between weakening the (entry) criteria or steadily delaying the introduction, then delay would be the preferred option," Rolf Peffekoven told the Berliner Zeitung daily in a release ahead of publication on Tuesday.

Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisers dubbed Germany's "five wise men," said a two-year delay would be better than delaying the project by five years, as advocated at the weekend by Saxony state premier Kurt Biedenkopf.
Biedenkopf is a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling Christian Democrats (CDU).
"I don't think that that (a delay) should now be five years. That is quite a long time," Peffekoven said.
"We need the euro to be a stable currency. For that the criteria must by strictly adhered to," he said.
Earlier on Monday, the German government restated its belief that the single currency project must go foward as planned in 1999.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann said that delaying EMU would jeopardise the project altogether.
Hausmann also restated the government's view that monetary union would start on schedule and that the future European currency, the euro, would be stable.
